name: Centre for British Progress — Rates and wrongs: technical appendix (25 March 2026), section 1, Tables 2 and 3
authors_basis: CenTax report footnote 46 (sources/centax-childcare-100k/raw/pages_layout.txt, printed page 99); the technical appendix itself names no authors
report_url_note: CenTax's footnote 46 cites the main report at https://britishprogress.org/reports/rates-and-wrongs-fixing-uk-tax-cliff-edges-and-tap (truncated in the PDF). On 2026-10-21 that slug, /reports/rates-and-wrongs and /reports/rates-and-wrongs-fixing-uk-tax-cliff-edges-and-tapers returned the site's 'Article Not Found' page, and britishprogress.org/reports carried no link to the report. The technical appendix, CBP's own publication of the numbers (CenTax footnote 47), is what is vendored.

pages_extracted.tool: pdftotext -layout (poppler 26.09.0), one PDF page at a time

citation: Centre for British Progress (2026), Technical Appendix: underlying modelling and analysis for each of the policies in the Rates and Wrongs paper, 25 March 2026.

model.name: CBP synthetic microsimulation of parents of nursery-age children
model.method: Children from ONS births for England (actual and forecast), each given a birthday and two parents with no siblings; parents' incomes drawn from the 2022-23 Survey of Personal Incomes (ages 25-44, opposite sex, partner correlation about 0.5). The subsidy is the maximum entitled hours at national average funding rates, plus Tax-Free Childcare (up to £2,000 in the model description; the tables assume £500). Two behavioural models are run separately: an endogenous pension choice with fixed labour income (Table 2) and an endogenous labour choice with no pension (Table 3, Frisch elasticity 0.3); in both an agent bunches at £100,000 only if it gains at least £1,000 (the friction).
model.method_basis: raw/pages_layout.txt: PDF pages 4-5 (sections 1.2.1-1.2.3), 7 and 9 (sections 1.3.4 and 1.4.5, the £1k friction), 8 (section 1.3.7, Table 2) and 10 (section 1.4.6, Table 3)
model.data: Synthetic: ONS births and the SPI 2022-23 (HMRC's sample of income tax records)

reform: Abolish the £100,000 cliff on Free Childcare for Working Parents and Tax-Free Childcare (the 'Abolish Cliff' row); the 1%-5% rows replace the cliff with a per-child opt-in taper on income above £100,000 (section 1.3.6).
period: Financial years 2026/27 to 2031/32, labelled as such

units.money: gbp — raw pounds (published in £bn to three decimals), as printed

sign_note: The appendix states no sign rule for its tables. CenTax's Appendix D (printed page 99) reads the abolition figures as raising revenue ('would raise between £130 million and £425 million in 2030'). The values are carried as printed and the sign is left unclassified.
coverage_note: Tables 2 and 3 in full: 72 cells. The 12 'Abolish Cliff' cells become claims; the 60 taper cells stay in data/externals with a tallied reason (no PolicyEngine construction in this lane).
diagnosis_upstream: CBP's model is not published as code; a divergence classified as an external-model issue becomes a comparison memo.
